home_map_description: Interactive map of the Province of Bukidnon in Northern Mindanao. The marker shows the Provincial Capitol in Malaybalay City, at about 8.1575°N, 125.1278°E.
home_history_precolonial: The highlands are home to the Bukidnon, Higaonon, Talaandig, Manobo, Matigsalug, Tigwahanon and Umayamnon peoples, the seven tribes of Bukidnon.
home_history_1850s: Under Spanish rule, the area becomes part of the province of Misamis.
home_history_1907: Act No. 1693 creates the province of Agusan with Bukidnon as a sub-province. Malaybalay becomes its capital.
home_history_1917: Act No. 2711 makes Bukidnon a regular province on 10 March, now celebrated as the province's founding anniversary.
home_history_1977: The provincial government holds the first organized Kaamulan Festival, a gathering of the seven tribes.
home_history_cityhood: Malaybalay becomes a city in 1998 (Republic Act No. 8490), followed by Valencia in 2001.
home_history_2012: Republic Act No. 10184 divides Bukidnon into four congressional districts, in effect from the 2013 elections.
home_history_card_tribes: Kaamulan comes from the Binukid word "amul", to gather. The festival brings the seven tribes to Malaybalay around the 10 March founding anniversary.
home_history_card_highlands: Mount Dulang-dulang in the Kitanglad Range, about 2,938 meters high, is the second highest peak in the Philippines. Bukidnon's plateau farms earn it the name "food basket of Mindanao".
home_volunteer_subtitle: BetterBukidnon.org is a civic project, not an official government website.

officials_meet_the_leaders_serving_the_p: Meet the leaders serving the Province of Bukidnon
officials_sp_intro: The Vice Governor presides. The Board has 10 Board Members elected by district and 4 ex officio members.
officials_ex_officio_note: Ex officio members sit on the Board because of the league or federation they lead. These seats can change mid-term; confirm current holders with the Sangguniang Panlalawigan.
officials_house_reps_intro: Each of the four legislative districts of Bukidnon elects one member of the House of Representatives.
leg_approval_in_session_desc: Members vote on the resolution in a regular or special session.
leg_committee_conducts_public_hearing_an: The committee studies the measure and may hold public hearings. A public hearing is required before a tax ordinance is enacted (LGC Sec. 187).
leg_committee_reviews_and_approves_the_p: The committee concerned reviews it. Some resolutions are taken up directly in session when the internal rules allow.
leg_committee_submits_findings_and_recom: The committee reports its findings and recommendation to the full Sangguniang Panlalawigan.
leg_detailed_discussion_and_debate_on_th: Members debate the proposed ordinance and propose amendments.
leg_ex_officio_desc: They sit because of another office they hold (Local Government Code, Sec. 467; the IPMR under the Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act).
leg_expressions_of_the_legislative_bodys: Expressions of the legislative body's will or opinion on specific matters, often used for commendations, requests, or policy positions.
leg_final_voting_on_the_proposed_ordinan: The Sanggunian votes on the final text. A quorum (a majority of all members) must be present.
leg_governor_approval_or_veto_desc: The Governor may veto it in writing within 15 days if it is beyond the Province's powers or harmful to public welfare. Items of an appropriation ordinance can be vetoed separately. With no action in 15 days, it is deemed approved (LGC Secs. 54–55).
leg_initial_reading_and_assignment_to_th: The title is read in session and the measure is referred to the committee concerned.
leg_learn_about_the_legislative_process_: Learn about the legislative process of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan
leg_local_laws_with_permanent_and_genera: Local laws of general and lasting application. Provincial ordinances apply throughout Bukidnon, within the powers the Local Government Code gives provinces.
leg_members_desc: The provincial board is the Province's legislative body. It is made up of the Vice Governor as presiding officer, 10 board members elected by district, and 4 ex officio members.
leg_members_note: Ex officio seats change when the federations elect new officers. Confirm the current membership with the Sangguniang Panlalawigan at the Provincial Capitol, Malaybalay City.
leg_ordinance_takes_effect_and_is_enforc: Unless it states otherwise, the ordinance takes effect 10 days after posting (LGC Sec. 59) and is enforced across the province.
leg_ordinances_and_resolutions_of_the_sa: How the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Bukidnon makes provincial ordinances and resolutions
leg_presented_to_the_governor_desc: The enacted ordinance goes to the Governor, who signs each page to approve it (LGC Sec. 54).
leg_presiding_officer_desc: The Vice Governor presides over sessions and votes only to break a tie (Local Government Code, Sec. 49).
leg_provincial_ordinances_enacted_by_the: Provincial ordinances: local laws passed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and approved by the Governor that apply across Bukidnon.
leg_public_participation_desc: Sanggunian sessions are open to the public unless a closed-door session is ordered by majority vote. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan holds regular sessions at least once a week (LGC Sec. 52), and residents can take part in public hearings.
leg_public_posting_and_publication_of_th: Within 5 days of approval, it is posted at the Provincial Capitol entrance and in at least two other conspicuous places. The gist of an ordinance with penalties is published in a newspaper of general circulation in the province.
leg_relation_barangay_desc: Barangay ordinances are reviewed by the city or municipal sanggunian, not by the Province (LGC Sec. 57). For a city, municipal or barangay ordinance, ask the city or municipal hall concerned.
leg_relation_desc: Bukidnon has 2 component cities and 20 municipalities. Each has its own legislative council.
leg_relation_outcome_desc: If the Sangguniang Panlalawigan finds that an ordinance goes beyond the powers of the city or municipal sanggunian, it declares the ordinance invalid in whole or in part. If it takes no action within 30 days, the ordinance is presumed consistent with law and valid.
leg_relation_review_desc: Within 3 days after approval, each city and municipal sanggunian sends the Sangguniang Panlalawigan copies of its approved ordinances and of resolutions approving local development plans and public investment programs. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan reviews them within 30 days of receipt.
leg_relation_who_desc: The Sangguniang Panlalawigan passes ordinances within the Province's powers, such as provincial taxes and fees, the provincial budget, and provincial programs and facilities. The Sangguniang Panlungsod of Malaybalay City and of Valencia City and the Sangguniang Bayan of each municipality legislate for their own city or municipality, for example on business permits, public markets and tricycle franchises.
leg_resolution_is_posted_publicly_and_tr: Resolution is posted publicly and transmitted to concerned parties
leg_resolution_is_scheduled_for_inclusio: Resolution is scheduled for inclusion in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan session
leg_resolutions_passed_by_the_sp: Resolutions of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan: formal statements of the Board's position or decision on a specific matter.
leg_secretary_to_the_sanggunian_and_pres: The Secretary to the Sanggunian attests it and the Vice Governor certifies it. Resolutions adopting a development plan or public investment program are also subject to the Governor's approval.
leg_see_lgu_list: See the list of cities and municipalities
leg_stepbystep_process_for_enacting_ordi: How a provincial ordinance or resolution is passed under the Local Government Code. Details follow the Sanggunian's internal rules.
leg_submit_the_proposed_ordinance_to_the: A board member files the proposed ordinance with the Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. The Governor may also propose measures.
leg_submit_the_proposed_resolution_to_th: A board member files the proposed resolution with the Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan.
leg_transparency_desc: Enacted ordinances must be posted publicly. This volunteer site does not list Bukidnon's ordinances and resolutions yet. For official copies, see bukidnon.gov.ph or ask at the Provincial Capitol.
leg_veto_override_desc: The Sanggunian can override a veto by a two-thirds vote of all its members. The Governor can veto a measure only once.
ord_empty_desc: See the Sangguniang Panlalawigan records at
ord_lgu_desc: Malaybalay City, Valencia City and the 20 municipalities pass their own ordinances. Their sanggunian sends approved ordinances to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within 3 days. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan reviews them within 30 days and declares invalid any ordinance that goes beyond the city or municipal sanggunian's powers; with no action in 30 days, the ordinance is presumed valid (LGC Sec. 56).
ord_page_desc: Provincial ordinances of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Bukidnon
ord_process_subtitle: The main steps under the Local Government Code (Republic Act No. 7160). Details follow the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's internal rules.
ord_process_title: How a Provincial Ordinance Is Passed
ord_records_subtitle: Provincial ordinances published on this site, newest first
ord_see_lgu_list: See the list of cities and municipalities
ord_step_1_desc: A board member files the proposed ordinance. It is read in session and referred to the committee concerned.
ord_step_2_desc: The committee studies the measure and may hold public hearings with the offices and sectors affected. A tax ordinance needs a public hearing before it is enacted (LGC Sec. 187).
ord_step_3_desc: Members debate and amend the measure, then vote on the final text with a quorum present.
ord_step_4_desc: The Governor signs each page to approve it, or vetoes it in writing within 15 days. With no action in 15 days, it is deemed approved (LGC Sec. 54).
ord_step_5_desc: The Sangguniang Panlalawigan may override a veto by a two-thirds vote of all its members (LGC Sec. 55).
ord_step_6_desc: Within 5 days of approval, the ordinance is posted at the Provincial Capitol and in other conspicuous places, and the gist of an ordinance with penalties is published in a newspaper of general circulation in the province. Unless it says otherwise, it takes effect 10 days after posting (LGC Sec. 59).
ord_table_caption: Ordinances of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Bukidnon
ord_what_is_p1: A provincial ordinance is a local law enacted by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (Provincial Board) and approved by the Governor, or passed over the Governor's veto. It has the force of law throughout Bukidnon, within the powers the Local Government Code gives provinces.
ord_what_is_p2: Provincial ordinances commonly cover provincial taxes, fees and charges; the annual and supplemental budgets (appropriation ordinances); provincial offices and programs; and provincial property, roads and facilities. Business permits, public markets and tricycle franchises are covered by city and municipal ordinances instead.
reso_empty_desc: See the Sangguniang Panlalawigan records at
reso_page_desc: Resolutions of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Bukidnon
reso_process_subtitle: The usual steps at the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Details follow its internal rules.
reso_process_title: How a Provincial Resolution Is Passed
reso_records_subtitle: Provincial resolutions published on this site, newest first
reso_step_1_desc: A board member files the proposed resolution, and it is included in the session agenda.
reso_step_2_desc: It is referred to the committee concerned, or taken up directly in session when the internal rules allow.
reso_step_3_desc: Members vote on the resolution in session, with a quorum present.
reso_step_4_desc: The Secretary to the Sanggunian attests it and the Vice Governor, as Presiding Officer, certifies it. Resolutions adopting a development plan or public investment program are also subject to the Governor's approval.
reso_step_5_desc: Copies are sent to the offices, agencies or local governments concerned.
reso_table_caption: Resolutions of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Bukidnon
reso_what_is_p1: A resolution is a formal expression of the opinion or will of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on a specific matter. Unlike an ordinance, it is generally not a law; it records the Board's position or decision.
reso_what_is_p2: Provincial resolutions are used for commendations, requests to national agencies, expressions of support or opposition, authorizing the Governor to sign agreements, adopting plans, and acting on the review of city and municipal ordinances.

budget_subtitle: How the Provincial Government of Bukidnon raises and spends public funds, and where to find the official reports
budget_major_development_projects_servin: Provincial projects are handled by the Provincial Engineer's Office; national projects by the Department of Public Works and Highways.
budget_sre_subtitle: What the Province collected and spent, and how to read the report
budget_empty_title: We are still gathering this information.
budget_sre_empty_desc: No official SRE figures for the Province of Bukidnon are published on this site yet. See the official sources:
budget_explain_sre_desc: The Statement of Receipts and Expenditures is a report each local government submits to the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF). It shows the income the Province actually collected and the money it actually spent over a period, by quarter and for the full year.
budget_explain_income_desc: Local sources are taxes the Province collects, such as real property tax and the tax on the transfer of real property, plus fees, charges and receipts from provincial enterprises. External sources are mainly the National Tax Allotment (NTA, formerly the IRA), the Province's share of national taxes.
budget_explain_expense_desc: Spending is grouped by purpose: General Public Services (administration, the Sanggunian, finance and support offices), Social Services (health, education, social welfare), Economic Services (agriculture, engineering, provincial roads) and Debt Service (interest and other charges on loans).
budget_explain_balance_desc: Net operating income is income minus expenditures for the period. The fund balance is what remains at the end of the period and carries over to the next one.
budget_howto_title: How to Read a Provincial Budget
budget_howto_subtitle: The budget is the plan; the SRE shows what actually happened.
budget_howto_ordinance_desc: The Governor prepares the executive budget, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan enacts it as an appropriation ordinance, and the Department of Budget and Management reviews it. Supplemental budgets follow the same path.
budget_howto_compare_desc: Put the budget next to the SRE for the same year. Large gaps between planned and actual collections or spending are worth asking about.
budget_howto_sources_desc: Compare local income with the NTA. A province that relies mostly on the NTA is more affected when national tax collections change.
budget_howto_required_desc: National rules set minimum allocations, such as at least 20% of the NTA for development projects (Local Government Code, Sec. 287) and a disaster risk reduction and management fund of at least 5% of estimated regular revenue (Republic Act No. 10121). Rules can change; check with DBM and DILG.
budget_infra_empty_desc: No list of provincial infrastructure projects is published on this site yet.
budget_dpwh_desc: National projects in the province are implemented by the Department of Public Works and Highways through its district engineering offices.
budget_dpwh_empty_desc: No DPWH project list for Bukidnon is published on this site yet. See the official DPWH website for national projects in the province.

budget_sources_desc: Under the DILG Full Disclosure Policy, local governments must post budget, financial and procurement documents in conspicuous places and on the Full Disclosure Policy Portal.

contact_notice_text: BetterBukidnon.org is run by volunteers. It is not the Provincial Government of Bukidnon and cannot process documents, payments, permits or complaints. For official requests, contact the Provincial Capitol using the numbers on this page or visit bukidnon.gov.ph.
contact_hotlines_note: Police is the Bukidnon Police Provincial Office at Camp Onahon, Malaybalay City. Fire is the BFP Malaybalay City Fire Station. Outside Malaybalay, your city or municipal police station, fire station or disaster office may respond faster. Except for 911, these numbers come from older directories, so please confirm them with the office.
